---
title: The API reference
description: Reference pages made from your code, and names in backticks that link to them.
order: 5
---

smalldocs writes a reference page for each module of your package. A reference page lists the classes
and the functions of a module, with their parameters. smalldocs reads what the code already says, so
you write nothing twice:

- The types come from the annotations.
- The description of each parameter comes from the comment beside it.
- The summary comes from the docstring.

The [Reference](../api/site.qmd) of this site is made from the code of smalldocs in this way.

## Write the code

Put one parameter on each line, with its comment beside it. Put the comment for the return value after
the colon of the `def` line. [fastcore](https://fastcore.fast.ai) calls these comments docments.

```python
def add(
    a: int,  # The first number
    b: int = 2,  # The second number
) -> int:  # Their sum
    "Add two numbers."
    return a + b
```

smalldocs shows other kinds of class in their own way:

- A dataclass shows its constructor, with the comment beside each field.
- A pydantic model shows its fields. The next section tells where the description of each field
  comes from.
- A `TypedDict` shows its keys, with the comment beside each key.
- A click command shows its function, with the comment beside each parameter. Then it shows a table of
  its options, with the help of each option. A click group shows the same.

If the `__init__.py` of a package defines functions or classes, the package has a page of its own.

### The fields of a pydantic model

For each field, the description in the reference is:

1. The `description` of the field, when it has one. This covers `Field(description="...")`, and a
   docstring under the field when the model sets `ConfigDict(use_attribute_docstrings=True)`.
2. Otherwise, the comment beside the field.
3. Otherwise, nothing, and `smalldocs api check` reports the gap, for example
   `Page.title: no description`.

A field with a description and a comment is documented, and the reference shows the description. A
comment for a tool, such as `# type: ignore` or `# noqa`, is not a description.

```python
class Page(BaseModel):
    """A page of Wikipedia: its title and the summary of its text."""

    title: str  # The title of the page
    extract: str = Field(description="The summary: the first paragraph of the page")
```

Each style is good for a different kind of model:

- `Field(description="...")` is data that pydantic keeps when the program runs. It goes into
  `model_json_schema()`, and so into an OpenAPI schema, a FastAPI page or the tool schema of an LLM. For
  a model that is the schema of an API, the description does the work of the comment and more. Use it
  there.
- The comment is lighter, and it reads like the comments of a function. For a model that only parses
  data, nothing else reads a description. There, the comment is enough.

## Turn on the reference

Add an `api` section to `_smalldocs.yml`:

```yaml
api:
  packages: [mypkg]                  # the importable packages to document
  out: api                           # the folder of pages, inside the site; `api` by default
  root: ..                           # the root of the repository, from the folder of the site
  source: https://github.com/me/mypkg/blob/main   # each entry links to its line here
  check: ["*.py", "tests/**/*.py"]   # more files that `smalldocs api check` holds to the convention
```

In a `_quarto.yml`, write the same section under `smalldocs:`, as `smalldocs.api`.

| Key | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `packages` | The importable packages to document. `package` with one name works too | None. An `api` section without it stops the build |
| `out` | The folder of the reference pages, from the folder of the site. It must be inside the site | `api` |
| `root` | The root of the repository, from the folder of the site. The globs of `check` start here | `..`, or `.` when the folder of the site holds `pyproject.toml` or `.git` |
| `source` | The address of the code. Each entry links to its line there | None: no links to the code |
| `check` | Globs of more files that `smalldocs api check` holds to the convention | None: only the packages |
| `linkify` | Names in backticks link to their entries. The top-level `linkify` wins over it | On |

Each build then writes a page `api/<module>.qmd` for each public module. A module is public when no
part of its name starts with `_`. The page has the name of the module without its package, such as
`site.qmd` for `smalldocs.site`. When two modules have the same last name, each page takes the full name.
A package whose `__init__.py` defines functions or classes gets a page too.

smalldocs notes the pages that it writes in the file `api/.smalldocs-api`. It deletes a page only if an
earlier build wrote the page and the new build did not. So a page of your own in the folder, such as
`api/index.qmd`, is safe.

To list the pages in the sidebar, use a glob:

```yaml
website:
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - section: Reference
        contents: api/*
```

smalldocs imports your package. So install smalldocs in the environment of the package. If the import
fails, smalldocs also looks in the root of the repository and in its `src` folder.

## The index of names

Each build also writes `_symbols.json`, in the folder of the site, before it builds the pages. It is a
JSON object. Each key is a name, and its value is the entry of that name, as a page and an anchor:

```json
{
 "Site": "/api/site.qmd#Site",
 "smalldocs.site.Site": "/api/site.qmd#Site",
 "Site.build": "/api/site.qmd#Site.build",
 "smalldocs.site.Site.build": "/api/site.qmd#Site.build"
}
```

smalldocs makes the index from the reference. For each class, method and function, it adds two keys:

- the name in its module, such as `Site` or `Site.build`
- the full name, with the module, such as `smalldocs.site.Site.build`

Two modules can have a function with the same name, such as `build`. Then the short name links to the
first one, in the order of `packages`, and then of the names of the modules. The full names link to each one.

smalldocs writes the file only when its content changes. Linkify then reads it.

## Links from the text

When the reference is on, a name in backticks can become a link to its entry, on every page of the
site. Linkify looks only at inline code, the text between backticks. It never changes the words of a
sentence.

The name must be in the reference, and it must look like code. A name looks like code when it has one
of these forms:

- a call, which ends in `()`, such as `inventory()`
- a dotted name, such as `Site.build` or `smalldocs.markdown.render`
- a name with an underscore, such as `package_modules`
- a name that starts with a capital letter, such as the class `Site`

A plain lowercase word, such as `main` or `check`, stays as code. Docs often name a branch, an option
or a command with such a word, and a link would go to the wrong place. To link a function, write it
as a call, `check()`, or with its module, `smalldocs.api.check`.

These names also stay as code:

- a name inside a link
- a name that the reference does not know
- a name with the class `nolink`, written as `` `Site`{.nolink} ``. Use it when a name looks like
  code but means something else, such as a `Site`{.nolink} in another program

## Use the reference at the terminal

```bash
smalldocs api build --dir docs        # write the pages and the index
smalldocs api module site --dir docs  # print one module as Markdown, for people and agents
smalldocs api list --dir docs         # every module, class, method and function, one line each
smalldocs api check --dir docs        # what is typed and documented, and every gap; exit 1 if any
```

`check` reports each gap in the code:

- a function without a docstring
- a parameter without a type or a docment
- a return value without a type or a docment
- a field of a pydantic model without a description or a comment
- a key of a `TypedDict` without a comment

The globs of `api.check` start at the root of the repository. In them, `*` stays inside one folder,
and `**/` is any number of folders, or none. So `*.py` finds the files at the root only, and
`tests/**/*.py` finds `tests/conftest.py` and `tests/unit/test_x.py`. `check` leaves out the files of
the packages in `packages`, because it already checks them as part of their package.

`check` names each file by its path from the root, such as `tests/test_x.py`. So the output is the same
on every computer:

```
tests/test_x.py:test_add: no docstring
```

Run `check` in your tests, or before each commit.
